catalogue.title: nesDS
catalogue.description: NES / Famicom emulator with a dedicated DSi build and TWiLight Menu++ integration.
install: For TWiLight integration, install its Virtual Console add-on, then copy nesDS.nds to /_nds/TWiLightMenu/emulators/.
Keep your own NES/FDS games separately; back up the existing emulator before replacing it.
requirements: Use the flashcart-compatible .nds asset for flashcarts. The .dsi variant adds a DSi title identity for compatible DSi launch/install routes. The extension alone does not set the CPU mode. The CIA asset belongs to a separate 3DS installation format and is excluded here.
Famicom Disk System games additionally require your own disksys.rom BIOS at the SD root.

catalogue.title: GameYob · mavica build
catalogue.description: Game Boy / Game Boy Color emulator, including Super Game Boy enhancements and scaling options.
install: Place gameyob.nds in a folder such as /roms/nds/homebrew/. Choose gameyob_dsi.nds only for a launcher with DSi-mode support.
Create /_nds/ at the storage root; this release saves its settings there. Select your own GB/GBC games in the emulator.
requirements: Use a launcher with working DLDI/storage access. The release notes acknowledge remaining Super Game Boy palette issues.

catalogue.title: NitroGrafx
catalogue.description: PC Engine / TurboGrafx-16 emulator with support for some CD-ROM², Super CD-ROM² and Arcade Card software.
install: Extract NitroGrafx.nds and launch it through your homebrew menu. Create /NitroGrafx/ or /data/NitroGrafx/ for settings and saves.
Keep your games in a folder of your choice. For CD titles, select your own System Card BIOS in Options → Machine → Select Bios and follow CDROM_readme.txt.
requirements: Some flashcarts need DLDI patching. No SuperGrafx emulation; game and CD compatibility varies. Published build is 0.9.1 even though the main-branch README says 0.9.2.
catalogue.artworkCredit: PC Engine logo supplied by FluBBaOfWard/NitroGrafx

catalogue.title: S8DS
catalogue.description: Sega 8-bit emulator for Master System, Game Gear, SG-1000 and related machines.
install: Extract S8DS.nds. Create /S8DS/ or /data/S8DS/ for settings and saves.
Place your own games and any system-specific BIOS files in a folder of your choice, then select them in the emulator.
requirements: Storage access may require DLDI patching on older flashcarts. Some emulated systems require a BIOS; compatibility varies. This is release 1.1.8, rather than the newer README version.
catalogue.artworkCredit: S8DS project logo supplied by FluBBaOfWard

catalogue.title: A7800DS
catalogue.description: Atari 7800 ProSystem emulator with per-game configuration and high-score support.
install: Copy A7800DS.nds to your card and launch with TWiLight Menu++ or Unlaunch on DSi, or a homebrew-capable flashcart.
Optional game folders: /roms/a7800/ or /roms/a78/. An optional 4 KiB BIOS named 7800.rom goes in /roms/bios/, /data/bios/ or beside the emulator.
requirements: Use your own .a78/.bin games. The published build supports NTSC; PAL is unsupported. DS/DS Lite has less CPU headroom than DSi; do not assume identical performance.

catalogue.title: StellaDS
catalogue.description: Atari 2600 VCS emulator with touchscreen cartridge selection, per-game settings and ARM-assisted cartridge support.
models: 3DS via TWiLight (DSi mode for ARM games)
install: Copy StellaDS.nds to your flashcart microSD or console SD and launch it. Tap the cartridge slot to select your own .bin/.a26 game.
Configuration and save data are created under /data/. Keep those files when updating.
requirements: Advanced DPC+/CDF cartridge types need DSi-class hardware running at 134 MHz for the intended experience. A flashcart normally runs in 67 MHz DS mode, including on a DSi/3DS. Older launchers may need DLDI patching.

catalogue.title: Wordle DS
catalogue.description: A native dual-screen word puzzle with daily words, statistics, mods and shareable results.
install: Copy WordleDS.nds to /roms/nds/homebrew/ (a suggested library folder), then open it in your homebrew launcher.
The game stores a completed result at /_nds/WordleDS/Wordle DS/share.txt; its statistics screen can show a QR result.
requirements: Use the NDS asset on flashcarts. The upstream .dsi asset carries a title ID for NTM; the CIA asset belongs to a separate 3DS install route. Neither is needed for the NDS download here.

catalogue.title: Aperture Science DS · portalDS
catalogue.description: A native Portal-inspired puzzle adaptation by smea, with graphics by Lobo. This is the original r1 release.
install: Extract the ready ZIP. Keep asds/ beside portalDS.nds; custom .map files go in asds/maps/ and controls are configured in asds/config.ini.
Use a NitroFS-capable launcher, such as hbmenu if the flashcart menu lacks support. This is a standalone adaptation, not the full PC game.
requirements: The author describes this legacy final version as buggy and incomplete. Modern launcher compatibility has not been hardware-tested here.

catalogue.title: Counter Strike DS
catalogue.description: A native Counter-Strike demake. Single-player remains usable; the original multiplayer server is closed.
install: Extract the hardware ZIP. Put its .nds on your card and soundbank.bin plus counter_strike_music.raw at the storage root.
On a DSi/3DS SD setup, highlight the game in TWiLight Menu++, press Y, then set Run in to DS mode.
requirements: Download the hardware archive, rather than the separate emulator package. Ad-hoc Ni-Fi multiplayer is unsupported; the publisher reports that the online server is closed.
catalogue.artworkCredit: Counter Strike DS screenshot published by Fewnity

catalogue.title: PUNCH-A-ROONEY!
catalogue.description: A native homebrew boxing game with a single-player championship and local multiplayer.
install: Copy Punch-A-Rooney.nds onto your flashcart microSD or prepared console SD, for example /roms/nds/homebrew/.
Launch it from the flashcart menu or TWiLight Menu++. Open Guide in the game for its controls.
requirements: Local multiplayer needs two compatible consoles running the game. The author notes that unexpected latency can occur.

catalogue.title: Homebrew Menu · hbmenu
catalogue.description: devkitPro’s file browser and launcher for native DS homebrew.
install: Extract the release and use BOOT.NDS with the bootstrap appropriate to your flashcart or existing homebrew route.
Place additional homebrew in /nds/ and keep required app data in the paths its publisher specifies. Read the release README before choosing a flashcart boot file.
requirements: This is a launcher for an already supported entry point, not a DSi exploit or a 3DS CIA installer. Bootstrap selection depends on the flashcart.
The original ready bundle also includes bootstrap.cia for a separate 3DS route. On DS/DSi use BOOT.NDS and the relevant flashcart bootstrap; do not install the CIA.

catalogue.title: CG NDS Input Test
catalogue.description: A native diagnostic for buttons, touchscreen, microphone and battery status.
install: Copy cg-input-test.nds to your flashcart microSD or prepared console SD, then launch it as native NDS homebrew.
No separate data folder is required. /roms/nds/homebrew/ is an optional organizational folder.
requirements: Battery information depends on hardware and launch mode; original DS hardware only exposes a high/low battery state.

catalogue.title: Switch - Basic Light
catalogue.description: A Nintendo Switch-inspired custom theme for TWiLight Menu++’s DSi interface.
install: Extract the theme directory into /_nds/TWiLightMenu/dsimenu/themes/ on the storage used by TWiLight Menu++.
Hold SELECT while starting TWiLight Menu++, choose the DSi interface in GUI Settings, select the custom theme and press B to apply.
requirements: Requires a working TWiLight Menu++ installation. “DSi” describes the menu interface, not an exclusive console model. Preserve any existing themes when copying.
catalogue.artworkCredit: Switch - Basic Light preview · Pk11 / DS-Homebrew skins
catalogue.author: Pk11

install: Extract the theme directory into /_nds/TWiLightMenu/3dsmenu/themes/ on the storage used by TWiLight Menu++.

requirements: Requires a working TWiLight Menu++ installation. “3DS” describes the menu interface, not an exclusive console model. Preserve any existing themes when copying.
catalogue.author: earedguitr, Void

catalogue.title: SpelunkyDS
catalogue.description: A native Spelunky remake focused on the cave levels, with generated layouts, traps and equipment.
install: Copy spelunkyds.nds to your homebrew storage, for example /roms/nds/homebrew/, then open it in a compatible homebrew launcher. This folder is a library suggestion, not a fixed app requirement.
Use the publisher’s 1.13DSi++ ready executable. The older README calls the launcher DSiMenu++; its successor is TWiLight Menu++.
requirements: This is an incomplete remake rather than the full commercial game. The project documents collision, item and crash issues; the release notes report stability improvements without guaranteeing crash-free play.

catalogue.title: Minicraft DS Edition
catalogue.description: A fan port of Minicraft with a lower-screen map, touchscreen inventory management and NBT saves.
install: Copy Minicraft-DS-Edition.nds to your homebrew storage, for example /roms/nds/homebrew/, then open it in a compatible homebrew launcher. This folder is a library suggestion, not a fixed app requirement.
Use writable SD storage for the game’s saves, and keep existing save files when replacing the executable.
requirements: This exact v1.0.0-beta.3 build is a beta. The original project lists unfinished features and interface work. No additional commercial Minecraft files are required.
catalogue.artworkCredit: ArthurCose · official Minicraft DS Edition overworld screenshot

catalogue.title: 2048 NDS
catalogue.description: A native 2048 number puzzle with a Professor Layton-inspired presentation.
install: Copy 2048-nds.nds to your homebrew storage, for example /roms/nds/homebrew/, then open it in a compatible homebrew launcher. This folder is a library suggestion, not a fixed app requirement.
Open the game to merge tiles and work toward 2048; no separate data archive is supplied with this release.
requirements: The author credits the presentation to Professor Layton assets. This is an independent homebrew puzzle; use the NDS release rather than a PC build.

catalogue.title: RaptorDS · Call of the Shadows
catalogue.description: A native DS port of the classic vertical shooter. The publisher’s ready package includes the DOS v1.2 shareware data.
install: Extract RAPTOR-NDS-V1.1.0.nds and copy it to your homebrew library, for example /roms/nds/homebrew/. Open that NDS file with a compatible launcher.

This exact NDS build embeds FILE0000.GLB, FILE0001.GLB and SETUP.INI in NitroFS: no external game-data folder is needed for the included shareware. Full-game data uses the publisher’s separate DOS v1.2 asset procedure.
requirements: The game build is RaptorDS v1.1.0 within the publisher’s MultiSys-V1.0.4 release. Other DOS revisions are incompatible; 3DS, Switch and Xbox packages are separate and excluded here.

catalogue.title: 3D Maze · Windows 9x port
catalogue.description: A DS port of the Windows 9x maze screensaver with a playable exploration mode.
install: Extract the FAT release and copy its data/ folder to the SD root. Place its NDS executable in your homebrew library.
Press START in the program to switch between automatic movement and player control.
requirements: The selected FAT build needs SD storage and keeps textures in external data files. The publisher also supplies a separate NitroFS package; this catalogue pins the FAT variant for customizable textures.

catalogue.title: 3D Pinball · Space Cadet DS
catalogue.description: A native Space Cadet Pinball engine port with standard and rotated screen modes. Bring your own game data.
install: Copy 3dpinball-nds.nds to your homebrew library. Put your own Windows 95 Plus / Windows XP Space Cadet game data in /data/SpaceCadetPinball/.
The v0.5 release adds Inverted rotation, using ABXY for the flippers. Keep the external data folder intact when updating the executable.
requirements: Full Tilt! Pinball’s CADET.DAT is not compatible with this port. Some table lights are incorrect in DS mode because images are downscaled; the author says this issue is absent in DSi mode. The download contains the engine, not the commercial data.

catalogue.title: Cereal Box Snow
catalogue.description: A creative particle simulator with snow, fire, rain, birds and fireflies.
install: Copy CerealBoxSnowNds1.2.0.nds to your homebrew storage, for example /roms/nds/homebrew/, then open it in a compatible homebrew launcher. This folder is a library suggestion, not a fixed app requirement.
Use the touchscreen and on-screen controls. In the NDS build, X or Up switches between attracting and pushing particles.
requirements: Select this Nintendo DS executable. The Windows and Linux releases are separate desktop apps and are not included in the console download.

catalogue.title: NitrousTracker · music studio
catalogue.description: A stylus-operated XM music tracker and sampler, with pattern editing and microphone recording.
install: Extract the ready ZIP. Copy nitroustracker.nds and the supplied songs/ and themes/ folders to your SD card. Launch nitroustracker.nds; debug and MIDI variants remain preserved in the original ZIP.
Use the app’s file browser to load or save .xm songs and .wav samples in folders of your choice. Keep copies of your songs before upgrading the app.
requirements: This pins the ready 0.6.5 GitHub release. Later builds, including native 3DS and beta releases, have separate packages; they are not substituted for this DS build.
Samples must be uncompressed 8-bit or 16-bit WAV. Memory available for samples is smaller in DS mode than in DSi mode.

catalogue.title: dsidl · DSi QR downloader
catalogue.description: A DSi-camera utility for downloading a file from a URL encoded in a QR code.
models: DSi / DSi XL · DSi mode only
install: Copy dsidl.dsi to the DSi SD card and open it with a DSi-mode homebrew launcher. A DS / DS Lite flashcart cannot provide its required camera and DSi Wi-Fi functions.
Configure Wi-Fi through System Settings → Advanced Settings. Scan a QR containing a URL, then choose the SD destination folder and filename in dsidl.
requirements: The publisher labels v0.1.1 as a prerelease. Requires a working DSi camera, SD access and a compatible router. Its dsiwifi library has router limitations; the author says WEP/open networks may not work. Hold SELECT at launch for connection logs.

catalogue.title: Sky
catalogue.description: A sky-themed menu designed for the blue DSi profile colour.
install: Extract the ready archive into /_nds/TWiLightMenu/dsimenu/themes/ on the storage used by TWiLight. Retain the skin’s own folder and original directory name.
Hold SELECT while launching TWiLight Menu++, choose the DSi user interface in GUI Settings, select this Custom Theme and press B to apply.
requirements: A working TWiLight Menu++ installation is required. DSi identifies the launcher interface, not a restriction to DSi hardware. Preserve other theme folders when copying.
catalogue.artworkCredit: kool_duck · official Sky theme preview via DS-Homebrew
catalogue.author: kool_duck
